questions.stem: This four-panel sequence shows dual pathways within the AV node, a premature beat, retrograde conduction, and an established loop. What arrhythmia mechanism is depicted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Triggered activity from early afterdepolarizations

choices.label: B
choices.text: AV nodal reentrant tachycardia, in which a premature beat sets up a reentry circuit using slow and fast AV nodal pathways

choices.label: C
choices.text: Complete AV block with a ventricular escape rhythm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enhanced automaticity of an ectopic atrial focus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sinus node dysfunction causing bradycardia

explanation.summary: AVNRT arises when a premature impulse blocks in the fast pathway, travels down the slow pathway, then conducts retrogradely up the fast pathway, creating a self-sustaining reentrant loop within the AV node.
explanation.whyCorrect: AVNRT arises when a premature impulse blocks in the fast pathway, travels down the slow pathway, then conducts retrogradely up the fast pathway, creating a self-sustaining reentrant loop within the AV node.

questions.stem: This four-chamber diagram highlights an abnormal muscular bridge (green) directly connecting the right atrium to the right ventricle, bypassing the AV node. What is this structure and its consequence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An accessory pathway (bundle of Kent) causing ventricular pre-excitation, as in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome

choices.label: B
choices.text: A normal moderator band conducting to the RV apex

choices.label: C
choices.text: A dilated coronary sinus draining the myocardium

choices.label: D
choices.text: An enlarged AV node causing first-degree block

choices.label: E
choices.text: A patent foramen ovale allowing atrial shunting

explanation.summary: An accessory AV connection lets atrial impulses reach the ventricle before the AV-node delay, pre-exciting the ventricle (delta wave) and providing a limb for reentrant tachycardia in WPW.
explanation.whyCorrect: An accessory AV connection lets atrial impulses reach the ventricle before the AV-node delay, pre-exciting the ventricle (delta wave) and providing a limb for reentrant tachycardia in WPW.

questions.stem: This diagram classifies arrhythmias by their site of origin above versus below the AV junction. On the surface ECG, what typically distinguishes an arrhythmia arising from the upper (supraventricular) site?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ST-segment elevation across all leads

choices.label: B
choices.text: A prolonged PR interval as a defining feature

choices.label: C
choices.text: A wide QRS complex from slow myocyte-to-myocyte spread

choices.label: D
choices.text: A narrow QRS complex, because the ventricles are activated through the normal His-Purkinje system

choices.label: E
choices.text: Absence of any P waves in every case

explanation.summary: Supraventricular impulses still descend the normal conduction system, so ventricular depolarization is rapid and the QRS stays narrow; ventricular-origin arrhythmias spread cell-to-cell and produce a wide QRS.
explanation.whyCorrect: Supraventricular impulses still descend the normal conduction system, so ventricular depolarization is rapid and the QRS stays narrow; ventricular-origin arrhythmias spread cell-to-cell and produce a wide QRS.

questions.stem: This ventricular cardiac action potential shows a long refractory period spanning depolarization through most of repolarization. What is the functional significance of this prolonged refractory period?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It sets the resting membrane potential during phase 4

choices.label: B
choices.text: It prevents tetanic (summated) contraction and re-excitation, ensuring the heart relaxes and fills between beats

choices.label: C
choices.text: It allows rapid repetitive firing to increase force by summation

choices.label: D
choices.text: It triggers calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum

choices.label: E
choices.text: It generates the pacemaker funny current in the SA node

explanation.summary: Because Na+ channels stay inactivated through the plateau, cardiac muscle cannot be re-stimulated until it has largely repolarized. This long refractory period blocks tetany and premature reentry, protecting diastolic filling.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because Na+ channels stay inactivated through the plateau, cardiac muscle cannot be re-stimulated until it has largely repolarized. This long refractory period blocks tetany and premature reentry, protecting diastolic filling.

questions.stem: The table pairs conduction system components with their intrinsic firing rates, which decrease from the SA node down to the Purkinje fibers. What is the physiological consequence of this gradient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The SA node normally drives the heart because its faster intrinsic rate overdrive-suppresses the slower distal pacemakers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Distal pacemakers speed up the heart during exercise

choices.label: C
choices.text: The AV node is the fastest and dominant pacemaker

choices.label: D
choices.text: All pacemakers fire simultaneously to summate the rate

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Purkinje fibers set heart rate because they fire last

explanation.summary: The fastest pacemaker sets the rhythm and resets slower sites before they reach threshold (overdrive suppression). If the SA node fails, a subsidiary pacemaker with its slower intrinsic rate takes over as an escape rhythm.
explanation.whyCorrect: The fastest pacemaker sets the rhythm and resets slower sites before they reach threshold (overdrive suppression). If the SA node fails, a subsidiary pacemaker with its slower intrinsic rate takes over as an escape rhythm.

questions.stem: The upper tracing shows an oscillation interrupting the plateau/repolarization; the lower shows one after the cell has returned toward rest. Which arrhythmia is classically caused by the upper (early afterdepolarization) mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Torsades de pointes in the setting of QT prolongation

choices.label: B
choices.text: First-degree AV block from nodal delay

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wolff-Parkinson-White reentry via an accessory pathway

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sinus bradycardia from vagal tone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Atrial fibrillation from pulmonary vein reentry

explanation.summary: Early afterdepolarizations arise during phases 2-3 when repolarization is prolonged (long QT), reactivating inward currents. They can trigger torsades de pointes; delayed afterdepolarizations (lower tracing) relate to calcium overload, e.g., digoxin toxicity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Early afterdepolarizations arise during phases 2-3 when repolarization is prolonged (long QT), reactivating inward currents. They can trigger torsades de pointes; delayed afterdepolarizations (lower tracing) relate to calcium overload, e.g., digoxin toxicity.
